answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with licensed ridge smokehouses: each identity tends one real juniper-smoke curing house on a named ridge, its fire logged daily by an independent food inspector who seals each batch with an opal-stamped tag. Random checks summon the keeper to tend that exact smokehouse on camera within hours, and one person cannot run two fires at once. The curing fee in outside money doubles per smokehouse on the same funding trail, so each extra fake identity costs another real smokehouse, another season of curing, another live keeper, and twice the prior fee.
